statement:
Let \(f(n, k)\) be the number of ways of distributing \(k\) candies to \(n\) children so that each child receives at most \(2\) candies. Determine the value of
\[f(2006, 1) + f(2006, 4) + \cdots + f(2006, 1000) + f(2006, 1003) + \cdots + f(2006, 4012).\]

Let \(ABC\) be an acute triangle. Inscribe a rectangle \(DEFG\) in this triangle such that \(D \in AB\), \(E \in AC\), \(F \in BC\), \(G \in BC\). Describe the locus of the intersections of the diagonals of all such rectangles \(DEFG\).

In a rectangular array of nonnegative reals with \(m\) rows and \(n\) columns, each row and each column contains at least one positive element. Moreover, if a row and a column intersect in a positive element, then the sums of their elements are the same. Prove that \(m = n\).

Consider a round-robin tournament with \(2n+1\) teams, where each team plays every other team exactly once and there are no ties. Three teams \(X\), \(Y\), \(Z\) form a cycle triplet if \(X\) beats \(Y\), \(Y\) beats \(Z\), and \(Z\) beats \(X\).

(a) Determine the minimum number of cycle triplets possible.

(b) Determine the maximum number of cycle triplets possible.

The vertices of a right triangle \(ABC\) inscribed in a circle divide the circumference into three arcs, with the right angle at \(A\) so that arc \(BC\) is a semicircle. For each of the three arcs, a tangent to the circle is drawn at the midpoint of the arc such that the point of tangency is the midpoint of the portion of the tangent intercepted by the extended lines \(AB\) and \(AC\). (For arc \(BC\), the tangent point \(D\) is the midpoint of the segment \(D'D''\) where the tangent meets lines \(AB\) and \(AC\) extended. Similarly define \(E\) on arc \(AC\) and \(F\) on arc \(AB\).) Prove that triangle \(DEF\) is equilateral.
